resources.string: Go to Android settings, tap permissions, and allow access to the camera.
Align the QR code provided from Thunderbird Desktop
The QR code was detected, but it contains invalid or unsupported data.
The other device can\'t be reached. Make sure both devices are connected to the same Wi-Fi network.
The accounts couldn\'t be read. Please start the transfer again on the other device.
This transfer isn\'t supported by this version of the app.
Couldn\'t connect to the Wi-Fi hotspot of the other device. Please try again, or use another way to transfer the accounts.
On the new device, open Thunderbird, go to Settings and select Import settings, then scan this QR code. Both devices have to be connected to the same Wi-Fi network.
Connect this device to a Wi-Fi network to transfer your accounts.
There are no accounts to transfer.
QR code with the data of the account transfer
No Wi-Fi network? This device can open its own hotspot for the transfer.
On the new device: Settings, Import settings, Scan QR code. The new device connects to this device\'s hotspot by itself; confirm the connection when asked.
This device can\'t open a hotspot for the transfer.
The hotspot needs the permission to find nearby devices.
The hotspot needs the location permission. The location itself is never used.
The hotspot couldn\'t be started. Switch off the Wi-Fi hotspot or tethering if it is on; on Android 12 and older location services must be switched on.
On the other device, copy the accounts as text and save them as a secure note in your password manager.
Open the note in the password manager on this device and copy its text.
Paste the text here and tap Import.
Computer, password manager vault, Thunderbird on the phone
Open the note in the vault of your password manager, copy its content and paste it into this field.
Help: how do I get the note?

Create it on the device where your accounts are already set up:

• Thunderbird on a computer: in the add-on “Transfer to Thunderbird for Android”, choose “Copy accounts for password manager”.
• Thunderbird on another phone: Settings → Backup → Copy accounts for password manager.

This copies your account data to the clipboard. Use it to create a new note in the vault of your password manager.
This text doesn\'t contain accounts from Thunderbird.
These accounts can\'t be imported by this version of the app.

Create a new note in the vault of your password manager and paste this content from the clipboard into it. Then, on the other device, open Thunderbird and go to Settings → Import settings → Paste accounts from password manager.
This is a lot of text. Some password managers limit the length of a note.
Copied. Only save it in a password manager and delete the note once the accounts are imported.
